entries.decision: qualified; regional card may be preserved but not as a directly named place
fixedWEBExcerpts: Moses gave to them, even to the children of Gad, and to the children of Reuben, and to the half-tribe of Manasseh the son of Joseph, the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites, and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan; the land, according to its cities and borders, even the cities of the surrounding land.
The children of Gad built Dibon, Ataroth, Aroer,

for the tribe of the children of Reuben according to their fathers’ houses, the tribe of the children of Gad according to their fathers’ houses, and the half-tribe of Manasseh have received their inheritance.
entries.findingJa: 32:33 explicitly names children of Gad (collective) and states Moses assigned Sihon/Og kingdoms/land to tribes. It does not present Gad as a place-name or a conquest/town/king list. Keep only if treated as an editorial regional label grounded in tribal allotment; distinguish from person and collective; no coordinate.

entries.decision: hold; exclude from adopted place runtime
fixedWEBExcerpts: Nevertheless Kain shall be wasted, until Asshur carries you away captive.”
But ships shall come from the coast of Kittim. They shall afflict Asshur, and shall afflict Eber. He also shall come to destruction.”
entries.findingJa: 24:22/24 speak of Asshur as a conquering/captive-taking power and one afflicted by ships; context personifies a people/polity. The existing collective ID person:asshur_349 better models the actor. The verses do not distinguish a geographic place-profile occurrence, so preserve raw draft/evidence but do not map/adopt place:asshur_109 without a separately supported geographic use.

fixedWEBExcerpts: With him the Reubenites and the Gadites received their inheritance, which Moses gave them, beyond the Jordan eastward, even as Moses the servant of the LORD gave them:
Moses gave an inheritance to the half-tribe of Manasseh. It was for the half-tribe of the children of Manasseh according to their families.
Their border was from Mahanaim, all Bashan, all the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, and all the villages of Jair, which are in Bashan, sixty cities.

Half Gilead, Ashtaroth, and Edrei, the cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan, were for the children of Machir the son of Manasseh, even for the half of the children of Machir according to their families.
entries.findingJa: 13:29–31 specify an allotment to Manasseh’s half-tribe and its area (Bashan, Gilead, Ashtaroth, Edrei); 13:8 places the parallel Reubenite/Gadite inheritance east of Jordan. The proposed East-Manasseh territory is an editorial regional aggregate, not a literal phrase in 13:29. If adopted use related and retain broad regional/ancient-historic qualifications; no exact point implied.

fixedWEBExcerpts: and the land of the Gebalites, and all Lebanon, toward the sunrise, from Baal Gad under Mount Hermon to the entrance of Hamath;
entries.findingJa: WEB renders the place-name as “the entrance of Hamath”; this is the translation-form of Lebo-Hamath, not an absent name. Direct linkage is supported; do not infer a modern archaeological point from this verse.

fixedWEBExcerpts: and to the kings who were on the north, in the hill country, in the Arabah south of Chinneroth, in the lowland, and in the heights of Dor on the west,
entries.findingJa: WEB renders Naphoth-Dor as “the heights of Dor.” The text explicitly includes this translated feature in a list of northern areas; the current map exclusion as absent candidate wording misses this translation correspondence. Modern point remains unproven.
